capabilities.reason: Offline construction only: no model call, tool execution or external service verification.

description: Execute a shell command and return its output. Use this for tests, builds, package commands, git commands, and other process execution. Prefer read_file/find_files/grep for inspection and apply_patch/write_file/edit_file for file changes instead of cat, shell find/grep, echo, or sed. Use -y or --yes flags to avoid interactive prompts. On Unix, commands run through bash by default; pass shell='sh' or shell='zsh' when needed. For long-running or interactive commands, pass yield_time_ms; if the command keeps running, exec returns a session_id that can be polled or written to with write_stdin. Output is truncated at 10 000 chars; timeout defaults to 60s.

function.name: exec

login.description: Whether to run bash/zsh with login shell semantics (default false).

max_output_chars.description: Maximum output characters to return when yield_time_ms is used (default 10000, max 50000).

max_output_tokens.description: Compatibility alias for max_output_chars. The current runtime uses a character budget.

shell.description: Override the Unix shell only when needed. Omit to use bash by default. Pass 'sh' for POSIX sh or 'zsh' for zsh-specific syntax.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. Increase for long-running commands like compilation or installation (default 60, max 600).

working_dir.description: Optional working directory for the command

yield_time_ms.description: Optional milliseconds to wait before returning output. When set, a still-running command returns a session_id that can be polled or written to with write_stdin. Omit this field to keep one-shot exec behavior.
